title: SDK client convergence: streaming-aware contracts, pagination, and retry guarantees
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD for aligning Python/TypeScript/Go client behaviors for paginated endpoints, streaming responses, and retry semantics. Goal: provide a single compatibility contract so applications can migrate between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments without behavioral surprises. This document captures requirements, acceptance criteria, known design trade-offs, and the minimal scope for the upcoming SDK release. It replaces ad-hoc per-language decisions with explicit guarantees and a deprecation path for legacy iterator APIs.
scope: In-scope: (1) Normative SDK behavior for pagination: cursor vs offset semantics, default page sizes, and transparent resumption. (2) Streaming API surface: server-side streaming over HTTP/2 and chunked HTTP/1.1, client-side backpressure APIs, and integration with existing async iterators. (3) Retry contract: idempotency markers, default retry windows, jitter/backoff policy, and error classification. (4) Compatibility matrix across Python, TypeScript, and Go: public method names, ergonomics, and semantic versioning guidance. (5) Acceptance tests and cross-language conformance harnesses. Out-of-scope: codegen for every language, UI/Console changes, runtime kernel-level optimizations, and enterprise-only deployment differences beyond configurable knobs.
out_of_scope: Large-scale refactors of existing SDK internals, language-specific idiomatic rewrites beyond minimal ergonomics, repository reorganizations, and feature work for embedding clients or CLI tools. Performance tuning of runtimes (batching/kv-cache) is handled by infra projects and not part of this ticket.
requirements: Pagination: Provide a canonical Pager abstraction in each SDK that supports both cursor-based and offset-based endpoints. Default to cursor-based for new endpoints; existing offset endpoints must keep behavior but expose a migration helper.
Pagination: Pager must expose a pull-style async iterator (or language equivalent) and a convenience synchronous builder when applicable.

Streaming: Define a StreamingResponse contract that exposes chunk boundaries, metadata events (open/close/error), and a pluggable backpressure API. Implementations must support both streaming over fetch/HTTP and gRPC where applicable.
Streaming: SDKs must surface a high-level helper for "line-delimited JSON" streaming and a raw stream for advanced use cases.

Retries: Default retry policy must be conservative: idempotent read operations retried up to 3 times with exponential backoff and jitter; non-idempotent writes are not retried unless caller supplies explicit idempotency key.
Retries: SDKs must provide a configurable RetryPolicy object and expose hooks for logging and metrics.

Compatibility: Public method names and parameter shapes for core endpoints (generate, embeddings, chat.stream) must be consistent across languages. Minor ergonomic wrappers allowed but must map to canonical options.
Compatibility: Semantic versioning policy: breaking changes require a major version bump and a migration guide in the SDK repo and docs.
Testing: Add an automated conformance test suite that runs a canonical set of pagination/streaming/retry scenarios against language SDKs in CI.
Docs: Document migration steps, examples, and a FAQ listing common pitfalls (backpressure, partial responses, cancellation).
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs implement the Pager abstraction and pass the paging conformance suite for cursor and offset endpoints.
StreamingResponse contract implemented and verified: backpressure honors consumer demand, metadata events surface correctly, and cancellation aborts the in-progress stream.
Default retry policy behavior validated against fault injection tests: idempotent operations retried, non-idempotent calls not retried without idempotency key.
Cross-language API parity checklist completed and reviewed by SDK owners (Python, TS, Go).
Conformance tests are added to CI and green for at least one build matrix per language.
PRD reviewed and approved by PM, Engineering Leads for SDK and Runtime, and Developer Experience (docs + examples).
Migration guide and code samples published on docs.redwood.ai and linked from SDK READMEs.
tradeoffs: Favor deterministic, measurable behavior over perfect idiomatic ergonomics in each language for this release. This means some language SDKs will get thin compatibility wrappers now and idiomatic rewrites later. We accept slightly higher surface area (additional helper objects) to avoid runtime ambiguity. Shipping conservative retries reduces user-visible errors but may require more user opt-in for aggressive retrying in high-throughput services.
